quick_skim.title: Cross-Subject Priors for Maximum a Posteriori Estimation of Latent Structure Influence Models in Motor-Imagery EEG With Few Trials
quick_skim.abstract: Coupled hidden Markov models such as the latent structure influence model (LSIM) describe how the sensorimotor rhythms of the two hemispheres evolve and interact during motor imagery, but subject-specific maximum likelihood (ML) estimates are unstable when few trials are available. This paper derives a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator for the LSIM whose conjugate prior equals the expected statistics of $λ$ pseudo-trials from a population model fitted to other subjects. The M-step remains in closed form, expectation maximization keeps its monotone ascent, and ML ($λ=0$) and the population model ($λ\to\infty$) are limiting cases. The prior strength was selected on 35 subjects of the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Dataset and applied unchanged to 70 held-out subjects and to BCI Competition IV-2a. With $λ=1$ the held-out log-likelihood exceeded that of ML in 61 of 70 subjects (Holm-adjusted $p=9.1\times10^{-8}$) and in all 70 subjects with five training trials per class. A prior learned only from the PhysioNet data improved the held-out likelihood of all nine BCI IV-2a subjects at five trials per class and reduced the error of the joint transition matrix by 61%. Decoding accuracy did not improve ($p=0.17$). Cross-subject priors therefore stabilize few-trial dynamic models of motor-imagery EEG, but they do not improve decoding, which in these data relies mainly on structure shared across subjects.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Subject-specific EEG models are unstable with few trials. The paper derives a MAP estimator for the latent structure influence model whose conjugate prior comes from a population model fitted on other subjects, keeping EM closed-form and monotone. Experiments on 35 PhysioNet subjects show stable motor-imagery decoding, offering a reusable cross-subject prior strategy.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对小样本条件下被试特定EEG模型估计不稳定、难以泛化的问题，本文为潜结构影响模型推导了最大后验估计器，其共轭先验等价于来自其他被试总体模型的伪试次统计量，从而在保持EM闭式更新与单调上升的同时引入跨被试信息。在PhysioNet数据集35名被试上的实验表明该方法能在试次稀少时稳定运动想象解码，为跨被试先验迁移提供了可复用的思路。

quick_skim.title: EE-Motion: An EEG-based Web Architecture for Live Affective Music Recommendation
quick_skim.abstract: Music listening is intrinsically tied to emotion, which drifts continuously within a single session. Although modern browsers interface with wearable brain-computer interfaces, recommendation systems remain structured around discrete logs and lack the infrastructure to integrate continuous physiological signals. Furthermore, existing affect-aware models rely on static user profiles and offline training, failing to serve anonymous newcomers without model retraining. We present a web platform that resolves both challenges. Pairing with a consumer electroencephalogram (EEG) headband over Web Bluetooth, the system captures live EEG, mapping frontal alpha asymmetry and arousal index to normalized valence-arousal proxy coordinates on Russell's circumplex plane. Driven by these coordinates, an affective adapter unifies structurally diverse recommendation backbones under a shared live scoring mechanism. By parameterizing anonymous visitors through a few favorite tracks, the module recommends tracks conditioned on live proxy coordinates. This demonstrates that real-time EEG-derived control signals can steer recommendations without persistent user tables or model retraining.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: EEG headband captures live affective signals mapped to valence-arousal for emotion-aware BCI
